problemStatement.formal: For f : ℝ → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ (n+1) f and a < b, there exists c ∈ (a,b) such that f(b) - T_n(b) = f^(n+1)(c)/(n+1)! · (b-a)^(n+1)
problemStatement.plain: Taylor's theorem with Lagrange remainder: any sufficiently smooth function equals its nth-degree Taylor polynomial plus an exact remainder term involving the (n+1)th derivative at some intermediate point.
whyMatters: Higher-order generalization of the Mean Value Theorem
Foundation for approximation theory and numerical analysis
Key tool in analysis for controlling function behavior

knowledge.progressSummary: SURVEYED: Created formalization with Taylor polynomial definition, Lagrange remainder axiom, and proved MVT is the n=0 case. 1 axiom (the Lagrange form), 0 sorries.
